result.sentence: This project is eligible for Fast Track, up to 3,000 kW.

work.method: Above 20 MW: the large generator procedures. A listed inverter-based system of 10 kW or less: the 10 kW Inverter Process (§ 1.1.1). Above 69 kV: not eligible for Fast Track. A synchronous or induction machine: Fast Track up to 2 MW. A listed inverter-based system: Fast Track up to the § 2.1 ceiling for its voltage, higher on a mainline within 2.5 electrical circuit miles of the substation. Anything else goes to the § 3 study process.
steps: At 5 kV to under 15 kV, a certified inverter-based system is eligible up to 3,000 kW on a mainline within 2.5 electrical circuit miles of the substation (§ 2.1).
Eligibility is not a pass: the utility still runs the Fast Track screens, and a project that fails them can go to supplemental review or the study process (§ 2.1).
Initial review of the screens: 15 business days from a complete application (§ 2.2).
Agreement after passing, or failing but still interconnectable: 5 business days (§§ 2.2.2 to 2.2.3).
Customer options meeting after an indeterminate failure: 10 business days (§ 2.2.4).
Supplemental review, if you elect and pay for it: 30 business days from the deposit (§ 2.4).
A pre-application report for one point of interconnection costs $300 and is due in 20 business days (§ 1.2). It holds the line-section data the screens use.
Utilities may post their own schedules that supersede these. gridprims does not file, submit, or track an application: you file with the utility.
assumptions: The project connects under procedures that follow FERC's pro forma; many utilities use a state version instead.
